newsitem.title: UK: N. Ireland police probe IRA bomb alerts.
newsitem.headline: N. Ireland police probe IRA bomb alerts.

text.p: British forces sealed off streets in Belfast on Wednesday after IRA guerrillas said they had abandoned two mortar bombs.
The Irish Republican Army using a code-word in statements to media said one device had failed to explode near a police base and guerrillas had dumped a second after encountering army patrols.
Police said both areas were being sealed off as a precaution as British army bomb experts prepared to move in to examine the devices.

The guerrillas, who are fighting to end Britain's rule over Northern Ireland and unite the province with Ireland, said one device, near the heavily fortified Andersonstown police base in the heart of Catholic west Belfast, had been aimed at a passing police and army patrol.
A telephone caller to media newsrooms late on Wednesday said that it had failed to detonate but that "our technicians have made sure everything is safe".
Later the guerrillas said that they had abandoned a car containing what they described as a powerful Mark 15 mortar on the Antrim Road in north Belfast.
The IRA said the mortar had not been primed to explode, indicating that it was in transit to a target.
Security sources said they would be moving in slowly to the vehicle in case of booby trap devices, a favourite ploy of the IRA.
Joe Hendron, a nationalist legislator with the Catholic Social Democratic and Labour Party, condemned the incidents and called on the IRA to call off a war that has intensified over recent months.
"The people are so very very tired of all this and they do want the republican leadership to call all this off and genuinely to go down the road of peace," he told BBC radio.
Police said that they were probing an attack by men who said they were from the IRA on a 16-year-old girl in Armagh city 30 miles west of Belfast.

They said two mem claiming to be from the organisation took her from a taxi office before midnight on Wednesday to a housing estate where they tied her to a lamp post. "She was slapped about the face by her attackers. Her hair was cut and paint was poured over her."

The incidents come at a time of tension in Northern Ireland. IRA guerrillas have refused Anglo-Irish demands that they abandon a 28-year-old war to get their Sinn Fein political wing into peace talks.
